questions.q: Coefficient of thermal conductivity is the product of heat, distance and reciprocal of (area $\times$ difference in temperature $\times$ time). The new value of a unit of coefficient of thermal conductivity, if fundamental units are $21.6\text{kg}$, \text{1 decimetre}, \text{4 K} and \text{1 minute}will be ______ $\times {10}^{- 6}$ new units.
questions.solution:
Coefficient of thermal conductivity, $k = \dfrac{Q \times l}{A \times \Delta \theta \times t}$

$⇒ K = \dfrac{\dfrac{m{l}^{2}}{{t}^{2}} \times l}{{l}^{2} \times \Delta\theta \times t}$

$⇒ K = \dfrac{m \times l}{\Delta\theta \times {t}^{3}} = \dfrac{21.6 \times 0.1}{4 \times {\left(60\right)}^{3}}$

$= 2.5 \times {10}^{- 6}$ new units

questions.q: The density of a sphere is measured by measuring the mass and diameter. If it is known that the maximum percentage errors in the measurement of mass and diameter are $2 %$ and $3 %$ respectively then the maximum percentage error in the measurement of density is
questions.solution:
The density can be computed by

$ρ = \dfrac{m}{v} = \dfrac{m}{\dfrac{{\pi d}^{3}}{6}}$

or $ρ ∝ \dfrac{m}{{d}^{3}}$

$∴ \dfrac{∆ ρ}{ρ} \times 100 % = \dfrac{∆ m}{m} \times 100 % + 3\dfrac{∆ d}{d} \times 100 %$

or $\dfrac{∆ ρ}{ρ} \times 100 = 2 + 3 \times 3 = 11$

Hence, the percentage error in measurement of density is $11 %$
